summary: Client only. HTML pages over the game, from a file your resource ships, kcds://resources/<resource>/<path>, or an http(s) address. A page sends with window.sendToGame(name, json), and what you send with Web.emit arrives as a window event with the data in event.detail. A resource can work only with its own views. Through Events.on, your resource also hears events about its views, each giving one object with `viewId`: webViewOpened (url), webViewLoading (url, isMainFrame), webViewReady (url, when the main frame has loaded), webViewFailed (url, description such as ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED, errorCode, isMainFrame), webViewNavigated, webViewConsole (message, source, line), webViewFocus, webViewUnfocused (reason 'escape': Escape on a focused screen in the world gave the game its input back) and more. A missing file gives ERR_HTTP_RESPONSE_CODE_FAILURE, as does a kcds:// file the resource runtime did not answer within 30 seconds, so a page that cannot load always reports it. To reload a failed page, see navigate.

open.summary: Opens a web view and returns its id. Throws while the browser is not ready. A view ends with `close`, its resource stopping, the player's connection ending, or a restart of the resource runtime after a browser failure, after which your scripts load again and can recreate it.

params.options: Optional: `x`, `y`, `width` and `height` in pixels; `zIndex`; `visible`, default true; `focus`, default false, which gives it the keyboard. With no or zero `width` and `height`, it fills the screen, as does a view at 0, 0 with the size from Web.screenSize(). Both follow the game's resolution, so a responsive page lays itself out again. `anchor: 'center'`, with `width` and `height`, keeps it centred as its size changes and within the edges. `resize` keeps it anchored, and `move` ends that.

open.exampleLua:
-- client
local Web, Controls = kcds.ui.Web, kcds.ui.Controls

local shop = Web.open("kcds://resources/shop_menu/ui/index.html", { width = 800, height = 600, focus = true })
Controls.showCursor()

Web.on(shop, "buy", function(item)
  kcds.core.Events.toServer("menuBuy", item)
end)
Web.emit(shop, "gold", { amount = 120 })

hide.summary: Hides a view, which keeps running.

focus.summary: Gives a view the keyboard and mouse, or takes them back. Meanwhile, the third-person camera does not turn with the mouse.
focus.exampleLua:
-- client
local Web = kcds.ui.Web

Web.focus(view)
Web.focus(view, false)

anyFocused.summary: Whether a shown view of any resource has the keyboard and mouse, which lets you hold off your controls while the player works in another resource's page. It is read at each call, with no event.
anyFocused.exampleLua:
-- client
local typing = kcds.ui.Web.anyFocused()
print((typing and "a page has the keyboard" or "the game has the keyboard"))

isVisible.exampleLua:
-- client
local Web = kcds.ui.Web

if not Web.isVisible(view) then
  Web.show(view)
end

setBackground.summary: Keeps a view running without drawing it.

isBackground.summary: Whether a view runs without being drawn.

navigate.summary: Loads another page into a view.
navigate.exampleLua:
-- client: reload a page that failed, after a moment; only the main frame counts
local Web = kcds.ui.Web

local chatView = Web.open("https://chat.example.com/", { width = 600, height = 400 })

kcds.core.Events.on("webViewFailed", function(failure)
  if failure.viewId ~= chatView or not failure.isMainFrame then
    return
  end
  print("chat did not load: " .. tostring(failure.description) .. " (" .. tostring(failure.errorCode) .. ")")
  setTimeout(function() return Web.navigate(chatView, failure.url) end, 3000)
end)

move.summary: Moves a view on the screen.
move.exampleLua:
-- client: top right
local Web = kcds.ui.Web

local width = Web.screenSize().width
Web.move(view, width - 420, 20)

setViewWorldScreen.summary: Draws a view on a screen in the world, as a cinema screen or a notice board: in perspective with each frame's camera, the page as the screen's size and turn show it. It hides while the camera is behind the screen, a corner is behind the camera, or one of the game's menus or screens is open; other things in the world do not cover it. With `texture: true` the page goes into the world itself instead: into the texture of your own screen model at that place (streamed in your resource's stream/ folder and placed with Prop.spawn; see Assets), sRGB BGRA pixels (DXGI B8G8R8A8_UNORM_SRGB) as large as the page, best with its mip levels. The world then hides it behind hands, walls and people and lights it; open the view before the model appears. A focused view (focus) gets the mouse where it points on the screen, the pointer held on the screen, and Escape gives the mouse and keyboard back to the game (webViewUnfocused). null draws the view flat again. Throws a TypeError for a missing position and a RangeError for a size not above 0 or over 200 m.

params.screen: { position, heading, width, height, tilt, texture } or null: `position` its middle; `heading` the way its page faces, in degrees, 0 north and 90 east; `width` and `height` in metres; `tilt`, optional, degrees it leans back; `texture`, optional, true draws the page into your screen model's texture, or { width, height } names that texture's size (at least the page's, the page in its top-left corner): give each screen shown at once a texture size of its own, one pixel more is enough. A texture with its mip levels has them made again from each frame, which keeps text steady far away; `bar`, optional with texture, another of your views as wide as the page, shown above it on the same screen (an address bar: any site can show under it, as sites refuse to be framed). The texture is then as high as both; the screen's pointer and keys go to the part clicked.

setViewWorldScreen.exampleLua:
-- client: a screen in the village square
local Web = kcds.ui.Web
local screen = Web.open("https://example.com/board", { width = 1280, height = 720 })
Web.setViewWorldScreen(screen, { position = kcds.math.Vector3.new(128, 2048, 60), heading = 225, width = 8, height = 4.5 })

setViewWorldPosition.summary: Makes a view follow a world point. Its top-left corner sits on the point each frame, moved by the offsets, and it hides while the point is behind the camera or off screen, or one of the game's menus or screens is open. null returns it to its own position.
setViewWorldPosition.example:
// client: a price tag over a market stall
kcds.ui.Web.setViewWorldPosition(tag, new kcds.math.Vector3(1652.5, 2151.5, 39), -60, -20);
setViewWorldPosition.exampleLua:
-- client: a price tag over a market stall
kcds.ui.Web.setViewWorldPosition(tag, kcds.math.Vector3.new(1652.5, 2151.5, 39), -60, -20)
setViewWorldPosition.exampleCs:
// client: a price tag over a market stall
Web.SetViewWorldPosition(tag, new Vector3(1652.5, 2151.5, 39), -60, -20);

on.summary: Listens for an event a page sends with window.sendToGame(name, json). The handler receives the parsed payload.
on.exampleLua:
-- client
kcds.ui.Web.on(view, "buy", function(item)
  kcds.core.Events.toServer("shop:buy", item)
end)

off.summary: Removes a handler, or all of an event's if none is given.

emit.summary: Sends an event to a page, where it arrives as a window CustomEvent with the payload in `detail`.

worldScreens.summary: Your resource's views on screens in the world, as setViewWorldScreen put them: each { viewId, position (its middle), heading, width, height, tilt, texture }. Several screens can show at once; each one drawn into a model's texture needs a page size of its own (the game's texture is found by its size).
worldScreens.exampleLua:
-- client
for _, screen in ipairs(kcds.ui.Web.worldScreens()) do
  print("view " .. tostring(screen.viewId) .. ": " .. tostring(screen.width) .. " x " .. tostring(screen.height) .. " m")
end

nearestWorldScreen.summary: The id of your resource's screen in the world nearest a point (the player's position, a camera's), measured to the nearest spot of its surface, or null when none is within range. Focus that one view to work one screen of many: it gets its own pointer and the keyboard, and Escape gives them back.

params.range: Optional: the farthest a screen may be, in metres. No limit by default.

nearestWorldScreen.exampleLua:
-- client: F8 works the screen in front of the player
local Web = kcds.ui.Web
kcds.ui.Key.bind("f8", function()
  local me = kcds.players.LocalPlayer and kcds.players.LocalPlayer.position
  local screen = me and Web.nearestWorldScreen(me, 15) or nil
  if screen ~= nil then
    Web.focus(screen, true)
  end
end)

screenSize.summary: The game window's size in pixels. It changes with the resolution, and `gameResolutionChanged` tells you when. Full-screen views and those with `anchor: 'center'` follow it on their own; see open.
screenSize.exampleLua:
-- client
local width, height = kcds.ui.Web.screenSize().width, kcds.ui.Web.screenSize().height
